1.explanation: The reproduce code renders two Menu examples: one uses <Menu.Group> and the other a <Menu.SubMenu>. In both cases we introduce an explicit text child (the {' '} expression) before the first <Menu.Item>. Under the hood, the Group/SubMenu component maps over all children (including that string node), expects each child to be a React element with props.className, and then crashes when it encounters the string. This minimal example reproduces the exact "Cannot read property 'className' of undefined" error shown in the screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: In the Menu component, when you place any literal whitespace (for example a space or newline) immediately inside a <Menu.Group> or <Menu.SubMenu> before the first <Menu.Item>, that whitespace becomes a child text node. The Group/SubMenu’s render logic blindly maps over all children (including that text node), treating it like a menu item object. This leads to an undefined child object and a crash with "Cannot read property 'className' of undefined".
